facts.statement: The genus Giganotosaurus was described by Coria and Salgado in 1995.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Coria & Salgado, 1995

facts.statement: The species Giganotosaurus carolinii was named by Coria and Salgado in 1995.
facts.quote: authority: Coria & Salgado, 1995

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Giganotosaurus was discovered in the Candeleros Formation of Patagonia in 1993.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was discovered in the Candeleros Formation of Patagonia in 1993

facts.statement: The fossil hunter Rubén Darío Carolini discovered the first remains of Giganotosaurus in 1993 while driving a dune buggy near Villa El Chocón in Argentina.
facts.quote: In 1993, the amateur Argentine fossil hunter Rubén Darío Carolini discovered the tibia (lower leg bone) of a theropod dinosaur while driving a dune buggy in the badlands near Villa El Chocón, in the Neuquén province of Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: Paleontologists Rodolfo Coria and Leonardo Salgado announced the discovery of Giganotosaurus at a meeting in 1994.
facts.quote: The discovery was announced by the paleontologists Rodolfo Coria and Leonardo Salgado at a Society of Vertebrate Paleontology meeting in 1994

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Giganotosaurus preserves almost 70% of the skeleton.
facts.quote: The specimen preserved almost 70% of the skeleton

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Giganotosaurus is housed in the Ernesto Bachmann Paleontological Museum in Villa El Chocón, which opened in 1995.
facts.quote: The holotype skeleton is now housed in the Ernesto Bachmann Paleontological Museum (where it is catalogued as specimen MUCPv-Ch1) in Villa El Chocón, which was inaugurated in 1995 at the request of Carolini.

facts.statement: In 1998, a partial left dentary bone containing teeth was assigned to Giganotosaurus by Calvo and Coria.
facts.quote: In 1998, the paleontologist Jorge O. Calvo and Coria assigned a partial left dentary bone (part of the lower jaw) containing some teeth (MUCPv-95) to Giganotosaurus.

facts.statement: The teeth of Giganotosaurus were compressed sideways and had serrations.
facts.quote: The teeth were compressed sideways and had serrations.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus had a strong neck and a proportionally small pectoral girdle.
facts.quote: The neck was strong and the pectoral girdle proportionally small.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus is thought to have been homeothermic with a metabolism between that of a mammal and a reptile, enabling fast growth.
facts.quote: Giganotosaurus is thought to have been homeothermic (a type of "warm-bloodedness"), with a metabolism between that of a mammal and a reptile, which would have enabled fast growth.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus was capable of closing its jaws quickly to capture and bring down prey with powerful bites.
facts.quote: It would have been capable of closing its jaws quickly, capturing and bringing down prey by delivering powerful bites.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the "chin" on the lower jaw of Giganotosaurus may have helped resist stress during powerful bites.
facts.quote: The "chin" may have helped in resisting stress when a bite was delivered against prey.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Giganotosaurus was larger than Tyrannosaurus, roughly equal in size, or if its largest size estimates are exaggerated.
facts.quote: Some researchers have found the animal to be larger than Tyrannosaurus, which has historically been considered the largest theropod, while others have found them to be roughly equal in size and the largest size estimates for Giganotosaurus exaggerated.

facts.statement: In 1997, Coria estimated Giganotosaurus to be 13.7 to 14.3 meters long and weigh 8 to 10 metric tons, larger than Carcharodontosaurus.
facts.quote: In a 1997 interview, Coria estimated Giganotosaurus to have been 13.7 (45 ft) to 14.3 (47 ft) m long and weighing 8 to 10 MT based on new material, larger than Carcharodontosaurus.

facts.statement: Sereno countered that determining a size range based on incomplete specimens was difficult, and both paleontologists agreed that aspects other than size were more important.
facts.quote: Sereno countered that it would be difficult to determine a size range for a species based on few, incomplete specimens, and both paleontologists agreed that other aspects of these dinosaurs were more important than settling the "size contest".

facts.statement: Based on a larger dentary bone, researchers proposed that Giganotosaurus had a skull up to 1.95 meters long, the longest of any theropod.
facts.quote: Calvo and Coria found the dentary to be identical to that of the holotype, though 8% larger at 62 cm (24 in). Though the rear part of it is incomplete, they proposed that the skull of the holotype specimen would have been 1.80 m long, and estimated the skull of the larger specimen to have been 1.95 m long, the longest skull of any theropod.

facts.statement: The first known fossil of Giganotosaurus was an incomplete tooth discovered near Lake Ezequiel Ramos Mexia in 1987 by A. Delgado and formally assigned to the genus in 1999.
facts.quote: In 1999, Calvo assigned an incomplete tooth, (MUCPv-52), to Giganotosaurus; this specimen was discovered near Lake Ezequiel Ramos Mexia in 1987 by A. Delgado, and is therefore the first known fossil of the genus.

facts.statement: Fossil tracks attributed to Giganotosaurus range from 36 cm to 50 cm in length with paces between 100 cm and 130 cm.
facts.quote: The largest tracks are 50 cm long with a pace of 130 cm, and the smallest is 36 cm long with a pace of 100 cm.

facts.statement: The footprints of Giganotosaurus are three-toed with large, coarse digits and prominent impressions of claws.
facts.quote: The tracks are tridactyl (three-toed) and have large and coarse digits, with prominent claw impressions.

facts.statement: A large dentary bone suggests that some Giganotosaurus individuals may have reached a weight of 10 metric tons, making them potentially larger than Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: They found the holotype specimen to have been equal to Tyrannosaurus in size at 8 MT (marginally smaller than "Sue"), but that the larger dentary might have represented an animal of 10 MT, if geometrically similar to the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that Giganotosaurus reached the maximum possible size for a strictly bipedal animal.
facts.quote: They concluded that these dinosaurs had reached the upper biomechanical size limit attainable by a strictly bipedal animal.

facts.statement: Scientists caution that size estimates for Giganotosaurus depend on the accuracy of reconstructing incomplete skulls and require more complete specimens for precision.
facts.quote: They cautioned that these measurements depended on whether the incomplete skulls of these animals had been reconstructed correctly, and that more complete specimens were needed for more accurate estimates.

facts.statement: A 2007 study estimated the Giganotosaurus holotype skull to be 1.56 meters long and the animal to weigh 13.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 2007, the paleontologists François Therrien and Donald M. Henderson found that Giganotosaurus would have approached 13 m in length and 13.8 MT in weight, while Carcharodontosaurus would have approached 13.3 m in length and 15.1 MT in weight (surpassing Tyrannosaurus), and estimated the Giganotosaurus holotype skull to have been 1.56 m long.

facts.statement: Experts note that larger Giganotosaurus individuals may yet be found, similar to how it took nearly a century to discover the famous 'Sue' Tyrannosaurus specimen.
facts.quote: He conceded that with only one good Giganotosaurus specimen known, it is possible that larger individuals will be found, as it took most of a century to find "Sue" after Tyrannosaurus was discovered.

facts.statement: Extrapolations from a related species suggest the Giganotosaurus skull was 1.634 meters long, making it one of the largest theropod skulls known.
facts.quote: In 2022, Juan I. Canale and colleagues described the large carcharodontosaurid Meraxes, which has the most completely known Carcharodontosaurine skull, with an estimated length of 1.27 m. Extrapolating from that skull, they estimated the skull of Giganotosaurus to have been 1.634 m long, making it one of the largest known theropod skulls.

facts.statement: Recent analysis of pelvic dimensions supports an original 1995 estimate that Giganotosaurus was 12.5 meters long.
facts.quote: Based on this idea, he found Giganotosaurus to have been 12.5 m long, identical to the estimate proposed in the 1995 description.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Giganotosaurus has been estimated to be between 12 and 13 meters long.
facts.quote: Length estimates for the holotype specimen have varied between 12 and 13 m

facts.statement: The skull of the holotype specimen is estimated to be between 1.53 and 1.80 meters long.
facts.quote: a skull between 1.53 and 1.80 m long

facts.statement: The femur of the holotype specimen measures between 1.365 and 1.43 meters in length.
facts.quote: a femur (thigh bone) between 1.365 and 1.43 m long

facts.statement: Weight estimates for the holotype specimen range from 4.2 to 13.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: and a weight between 4.2 and 13.8 MT

facts.statement: Fused sutures in the braincase indicate that the holotype specimen was a mature adult.
facts.quote: Fusion of sutures (joints) in the braincase indicates the holotype specimen was a mature individual

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus is often compared to an oversized version of the genus Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Giganotosaurus has been compared to an oversized version of the well-known genus Allosaurus

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Giganotosaurus possessed four tooth sockets, a feature shared with Acrocanthosaurus and Sinraptor.
facts.quote: The premaxilla (frontmost bone of the upper jaw) had four alveoli (tooth sockets), as in Acrocanthosaurus and Sinraptor

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Giganotosaurus contained a tooth row measuring 92 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The maxilla of the upper jaw had a 92 cm long tooth row

facts.statement: The nasal bone of Giganotosaurus was extremely rough and wrinkled, covering its entire upper surface.
facts.quote: The nasal bone was very rugose (rough and wrinkled), and these rugosities continued backwards, covering the entire upper surface of this bone

facts.statement: A prominent, rough crest or horn pointed backward above the eye socket on the lacrimal bone.
facts.quote: The lacrimal bone in front of the eye had a prominent, rugose crest (or horn) that pointed up at a backwards angle

facts.statement: The crest on the lacrimal bone was ridge-like and featured deep grooves.
facts.quote: The crest was ridge-like, and had deep grooves

facts.statement: The quadrate bone at the rear of the skull measured 44 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The quadrate bone at the back of the skull was 44 cm long

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that each half of the lower jaw may have contained twelve tooth sockets.
facts.quote: It is possible that each dentary had twelve alveoli

facts.statement: One of the teeth possessed between nine and twelve serrations per millimeter.
facts.quote: One tooth had nine to twelve serrations per mm (0.039 in)

facts.statement: The shoulder girdle of Giganotosaurus was proportionally shorter than that of Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: The pectoral girdle was proportionally shorter than that of Tyrannosaurus

facts.statement: The ratio between the scapula and femur length in Giganotosaurus was less than 0.5.
facts.quote: The ratio between the scapula (shoulder blade) and the femur being less than 0.5

facts.statement: The ischium bone was straight, expanded backward, and ended in a lobe-like shape.
facts.quote: The ischium was straight and expanded hindwards, ending in a lobe-shape

facts.statement: The femur was S-shaped and featured a very robust head pointing upward.
facts.quote: The femur was sigmoid-shaped, and had a very robust, upwards pointing head

facts.statement: The fourth trochanter on the femur was large and projected backward.
facts.quote: The fourth trochanter was large and projected backwards

facts.statement: Coria and Salgado originally classified Giganotosaurus as belonging to the Tetanurae clade rather than basal theropods like ceratosaurs.
facts.quote: Coria and Salgado originally found Giganotosaurus to group more closely with the theropod clade Tetanurae than to more basal (or "primitive") theropods such as ceratosaurs

facts.statement: In 1996, Sereno and colleagues placed Giganotosaurus, Carcharodontosaurus, and Acrocanthosaurus within the superfamily Allosauroidea.
facts.quote: In 1996, Sereno and colleagues found Giganotosaurus, Carcharodontosaurus, and Acrocanthosaurus to be closely related within the superfamily Allosauroidea

facts.statement: In 2006, Coria and Currie grouped Giganotosaurus and Mapusaurus into the subfamily Giganotosaurinae.
facts.quote: In 2006, Coria and Currie united Giganotosaurus and Mapusaurus in the carcharodontosaurid subfamily Giganotosaurinae

facts.statement: In 2008, Sereno and Stephen L. Brusatte united Giganotosaurus, Mapusaurus, and Tyrannotitan into the tribe Giganotosaurini.
facts.quote: In 2008, Sereno and the paleontologist Stephen L. Brusatte united Giganotosaurus, Mapusaurus, and Tyrannotitan in the tribe Giganotosaurini

facts.statement: In 2010, Paul listed Giganotosaurus synonymously with Carcharodontosaurus carolinii without further explanation.
facts.quote: In 2010, Paul listed Giganotosaurus as "Giganotosaurus (or Carcharodontosaurus) carolinii" without elaboration

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus is considered one of the largest theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Giganotosaurus is thought to have been one of the largest theropod dinosaurs

facts.statement: It is impossible to determine with certainty if Giganotosaurus was larger than Tyrannosaurus, which has historically been considered the largest theropod.
facts.quote: It is therefore impossible to determine with certainty whether it was larger than Tyrannosaurus, for example, which has been considered the largest theropod historically

facts.statement: Some researchers believe the largest size estimates for Giganotosaurus specimens may be exaggerated.
facts.quote: Some writers have considered the largest size estimates for both specimens exaggerated

facts.statement: The jaw of Giganotosaurus articulated far behind the neck attachment point compared to other theropods.
facts.quote: The jaw articulated far behind the occipital condyle (where the neck is attached to the skull) compared to other theropods

facts.statement: The curvature of the lower jaw indicates that Giganotosaurus had a wide mouth.
facts.quote: The curvature of the dentary shows that the mouth of Giganotosaurus would have been wide

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus teeth were compressed sideways, oval in cross-section, and had serrations on both front and back borders.
facts.quote: The teeth were compressed sideways, were oval in cross-section, and had serrations at the front and back borders, which is typical of theropods

facts.statement: The side teeth of Giganotosaurus featured curved ridges of enamel.
facts.quote: The side teeth of Giganotosaurus had curved ridges of enamel

facts.statement: The largest teeth in the upper jaw had pronounced wrinkles with the highest relief near the serrations.
facts.quote: The largest teeth in the premaxilla had pronounced wrinkles (with their highest relief near the serrations)

facts.statement: The brain of Giganotosaurus was similar to that of Carcharodontosaurus but larger.
facts.quote: A latex endocast of the brain cavity of Giganotosaurus showed that the brain was similar to that of the related genus Carcharodontosaurus, but larger

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus had a strong neck with a robust axis vertebra.
facts.quote: The neck of Giganotosaurus was strong, and the axis bone (the neck vertebra that articulates with the skull) was robust

facts.statement: The rear neck vertebrae of Giganotosaurus had short, flattened bodies with almost hemispherical front articulations.
facts.quote: The rear neck (cervical) vertebrae had short, flattened centra (the "bodies" of the vertebrae), with almost hemispherical articulations (contacts) at the front

facts.statement: The tail vertebrae of Giganotosaurus had elongated neural spines and robust bodies.
facts.quote: The tail (caudal) vertebrae had neural spines that were elongated from front to back and had robust centra

facts.statement: The coracoid bone of Giganotosaurus was small and hook-shaped.
facts.quote: The coracoid was small and hook-shaped

facts.statement: The tibia was expanded at the upper end with a wide articular facet for connection to the femur.
facts.quote: The tibia of the lower leg was expanded at the upper end, its articular facet (where it articulated with the femur) was wide

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus belonged to the subfamily Carcharodontosaurinae, which was likely restricted to the southern continent of Gondwana.
facts.quote: The subfamily Carcharodontosaurinae, in which Giganotosaurus belongs, appears to have been restricted to the southern continent of Gondwana

facts.statement: In 1999 and 2002, paleontologist Reese E. Barrick and geologist William J. Showers found that Giganotosaurus had oxygen isotope patterns similar to Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1999 and 2002, the paleontologist Reese E. Barrick and the geologist William J. Showers found that the bones of Giganotosaurus and Tyrannosaurus had very similar oxygen isotope patterns

facts.statement: The metabolism of an 8 metric ton Giganotosaurus was comparable to that of a 1 metric ton mammalian carnivore.
facts.quote: The metabolism of an 8 MT Giganotosaurus would be comparable to that of a 1 MT mammalian carnivore

facts.statement: A 2017 study suggested that skeletal loads were too great for adult Giganotosaurus to run, implying they were limited to walking gaits.
facts.quote: A 2017 biomechanical study of the running ability of Tyrannosaurus by the biologist William I. Sellers and colleagues suggested that skeletal loads were too great to have allowed adult individuals to run

facts.statement: While absolute bite force values in newtons were impossible to estimate, Giganotosaurus had a weaker bite force than Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Estimates in absolute values like newtons were impossible. The bite force of Giganotosaurus was weaker than that of Tyrannosaurus

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus had lower jaws adapted for slicing bites and likely captured prey using the front part of its jaws.
facts.quote: The lower jaws were adapted for slicing bites, and it probably captured and manipulated prey with the front part of the jaws

facts.statement: Coria suggested that a bonebed of Giganotosaurus relatives was the result of a catastrophic event and that the mix of ages indicated these large theropods hunted in packs.
facts.quote: In a 2006 National Geographic article, Coria stated that the bonebed was probably the result of a catastrophic event and that the presence of mainly medium-sized individuals, with very few young or old, is normal for animals that form packs

facts.statement: The Candeleros Formation containing Giganotosaurus fossils was composed of sandstones deposited in fluvial and aeolian environments.
facts.quote: The formation is composed of coarse and medium-grained sandstones deposited in a fluvial environment (associated with rivers and streams), and in aeolian conditions (effected by wind)

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus was likely the apex predator in its ecosystem, sharing it with sauropods like Andesaurus.
facts.quote: Giganotosaurus was probably the apex predator in its ecosystem. It shared its environment with herbivorous dinosaurs such as the titanosaurian sauropod Andesaurus

facts.statement: The genus Giganotosaurus was named by Coria and Salgado in 1995.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Coria & Salgado, 1995

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus carolinii is the only known species in the extinct genus Giganotosaurus, a carnosaurian theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Giganotosaurus carolinii (gr. γίγας [gigas] 'gigante', νότος [notos] 'sur' y –σαύρος [–saurus] "lagarto gigante del sur, de Carolini", su descubridor") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Giganotosaurus de dinosaurio terópodo carcarodontosáurido

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus lived between 99 and 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: que vivió hace entre 99 a 95 millones de años, en el Cenomaniano (inicios de la época Cretácico Inferior). en lo que hoy es la Patagonia Argentina.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus is one of the largest known theropods, estimated to reach lengths of 12 to 13 meters, a skull over 1.60 meters long, and a weight of 7 to 8 tons.
facts.quote: Es uno de los mayores terópodos conocidos; se cree que alcanzaba longitudes de entre 12 a 13 m, con un cráneo de posiblemente de más de 1,60m de largo y un peso aproximado de entre 7 a 8tn.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus is part of an intense scientific debate regarding the maximum sizes that theropod dinosaurs can reach.
facts.quote: convirtiéndose en parte de un intenso debate científico acerca los tamaños máximos que pueden alcanzar los dinosaurios terópodos.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus was likely the largest predator of its time, occupying the top of the food chain.
facts.quote: Debió ser el depredador más grande de su época, ubicándose en la cima de la cadena alimenticia.

facts.statement: It is probable that Giganotosaurus preyed on a wide range of saurischians, including giant titanosaurian sauropods.
facts.quote: Es probable que haya depredado una amplia gama de animales saurópsidos, incluyendo hasta gigantescos saurópodos titanosaurianos.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus used its keen sense of smell for tracking and its large jaws with long, flattened, serrated teeth as its primary weapon to cut and tear deep into the flesh of its victims.
facts.quote: Tenía como herramienta de rastreo su agudo olfato y como principal arma de ataque sus grandes fauces dotadas de largos y achatados dientes con bordes dentados, especializados para cortar y desgarrar profundamente la carne de sus víctimas.

facts.statement: The discovery of an almost complete skeleton provided enough fossil material to study the dinosaur's thermoregulation, brain anatomy, bite force, and potential speed.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de un esqueleto casi completo de esta especie ha entregado el material fósil suficiente para investigar en detalle algunos aspectos de su biología, como su capacidad de termorregulación y su anatomía cerebral; además de sus capacidades biomecánicas, como la fuerza de mordida y la velocidad potencial.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Giganotosaurus may have been a homeothermic organism with an active lifestyle and faster growth than cold-blooded reptiles.
facts.quote: Posiblemente se haya tratado de un organismo homeotermo y, por lo tanto, un animal con un estilo de vida activo y de crecimiento más rápido que un reptil de sangre fría.

facts.statement: Based on the holotype MUCPv-CH-1, studies estimate Giganotosaurus at 12 to 13 meters long, 6.1 to 6.9 tons, and over 4 meters high at the hips.
facts.quote: Basándose en el holotipo, MUCPv-CH-1, diferentes estudios a lo largo de los años han estimado al Giganotosaurus en un rango de entre 12 y 13 m de longitud, de 6,1 a 6,9 tn de peso, y con una altura superior a unos 4 m hasta las caderas.

facts.statement: The skull length was originally estimated at 1.8 meters but is now corrected to 1.56 meters after the reconstruction was proven erroneous.
facts.quote: La longitud del cráneo fue originalmente estimada en 1,8 m pero se ha demostrado que esta reconstrucción es errónea y actualmente se estima en 1,56 m.

facts.statement: The femur of Giganotosaurus measures up to 143 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El fémur, o hueso del muslo, mide hasta 143 cm de largo.

facts.statement: A second specimen, MUCPv-95, known only from fragments of the left jaw, exceeds the holotype's dimensions by 6.5% to 8% according to various calculations.
facts.quote: Además, existe un segundo espécimen, MUCPv-95, conocido solo por unos fragmentos de la mandíbula izquierda, que superan comparativamente la del holotipo en un 6,5% u 8% según distintos cálculos.

facts.statement: If the second specimen represents a larger individual, estimates project a length of 13.2 to 13.5 meters and a weight of 8.2 to 8.7 tons.
facts.quote: Esto podría indicar que el Giganotosaurus alcanzaba mayores tamaños. Los estimados han proyectado dimensiones de 13,2 a 13,5 m de largo y 8,2 a 8,7 tn de peso.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus was a bipedal predator with a large skull supported by a powerful neck, short forelimbs with three fingers ending in curved, sharp claws, and powerful hind limbs.
facts.quote: El Giganotosaurus era un depredador bípedo con un gran cráneo sostenido por un cuello poderoso, extremidades superiores cortas en proporción a su tamaño, provistas de tres dedos terminados en garras curvas y afiladas, y extremidades inferiores poderosas.

facts.statement: The hind legs of Giganotosaurus had a femur longer than the tibia, indicating strong support but not high speed.
facts.quote: Las patas posteriores del Giganotosaurus se caracterizaban por tener un fémur más largo que la tibia, lo que indica que sus piernas lo dotaban de gran soporte pero no de gran velocidad.

facts.statement: This suggests Giganotosaurus was an ambush predator or hunted slow prey such as sauropods.
facts.quote: Esto sugiere que era un depredador de emboscada o que cazaba presas lentas, como los saurópodos.

facts.statement: In the holotype, the femur measured between 143 and 136.5 cm, the tibia 112 cm, and the fibula about 84 cm.
facts.quote: En el holotipo, solo el fémur medía entre 143 y 136,5 cm de largo, la tibia medía 112 cm y el peroné unos 84 cm.

facts.statement: The head of the femur had a sigmoid curve shape and was thicker than the rest of the bone.
facts.quote: La cabeza del fémur tenía forma de curva sigmoidea y estaba más engrosada que el resto del hueso.

facts.statement: The neck was short and robust, forming a less marked natural curve than in other theropods, with the typical S-shape almost non-existent.
facts.quote: El cuello, corto y robusto, formaba una curva natural menos marcada que en los demás terópodos, con la típica forma de S casi inexistente.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae had high vertebral bodies but low spinous processes, suggesting the neck muscles were not as strongly developed as in tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Las vértebras del cuello presentaban cuerpos vertebrales altos, pero con una apófisis espinosa baja, lo que sería señal de que los músculos del cuello no estaban tan fuertemente desarrollados como en los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: The characteristic shape of the neural spines made the back of Giganotosaurus straighter than most theropods and less arched than in Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: La forma característica de las espinas neurales del Giganotosaurus provocaba que su espalda fuese más recta que las de la mayoría de los terópodos, menos arqueada que en el caso de Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The ribs were robust, forming an oval ribcage in frontal view that was more robust than in other carcarodontosaurids but thinner than in tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Las costillas eran robustas y construían una caja torácica ovalada en vista frontal, más corpulenta que en los otros carcarodontosáuridos, pero más delgada que en los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus possessed one of the largest skulls known among theropod dinosaurs, which was disproportionately large for its immense body size.
facts.quote: El Giganotosaurus tenía un gran cráneo, de los más grandes conocidos entre los dinosaurios terópodos, desproporcionado aún para su inmenso tamaño.

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Giganotosaurus held a row of teeth spanning a length of 92 centimeters.
facts.quote: El maxilar tenía una hilera de dientes que recorría un tramo de 92 cm en la mandíbula superior.

facts.statement: The square bone at the lower rear of the skull was 44 centimeters long and contained two pneumatic holes on its inner side.
facts.quote: El hueso cuadrado se encontraba en la parte posteroinferior del cráneo y articulaba con la mandíbula. Tenía 44 cm de largo y dos agujeros neumáticos en el lado interno.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus teeth were flattened and S-shaped from the side, narrow and compressed from the front, and oval-shaped from above.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Giganotosaurus eran achatados y curvados en forma sigmoidea en vista lateral, estrechos y comprimidos en vista frontal, y con forma ovalada desde la vista superior.

facts.statement: Each tooth of Giganotosaurus featured a retrocurved enamel covering with sharp serrated edges.
facts.quote: Cada diente, poseía una cubierta retrocurvada de esmalte con afilados bordes dentados.

facts.statement: The species name Giganotosaurus carolinii honors the amateur fossil hunter Rubén Carolini, who discovered the remains in 1993.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie tipo y única especie conocida, Giganotosaurus carolinii, es en reconocimiento al aficionado que descubrió sus restos en 1993, Rubén Carolini.

facts.statement: The genus name Giganotosaurus means "giant southern lizard" and is derived from Greek words for giant, south, and lizard.
facts.quote: El nombre del género hace referencia a su gran tamaño, y deriva del griego gigas, γίγας "gigante", notos, νότος "sur" y –saurus, –σαύρος "lagarto".

facts.statement: According to a 2016 study by Apesteguía et al., Giganotosaurus belongs to the family Carcharodontosauridae.
facts.quote: El siguiente cladograma se basa en el estudio de Apesteguía et al., 2016, mostrando la posición de Giganotosaurus dentro de la familia Carcharodontosauridae.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus lived during the Albian stage of the Cretaceous Period, between 113.2 and 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: After the discovery of another jawbone, the skull length was re-estimated at 1.8 meters, making it the carnivorous dinosaur with the largest known skull.
facts.quote: Poco después, junto al descubrimiento del dentario de otro espécimen, se re-estimó su longitud en 1,8 metros, convirtiéndolo en el dinosaurio carnívoro con el mayor cráneo conocido.

facts.statement: Unlike most theropods, Giganotosaurus lacked a sagittal crest on the top of its skull, and its jaw muscles did not extend to the cranial vault.
facts.quote: El Giganotosaurus no contaba con una cresta sagital en la parte superior del cráneo como en la mayoría de los terópodos y sus músculos mandibulares tampoco se extendían hasta la bóveda craneana.

facts.statement: The lacrimal bone in front of the eyes featured a prominent rough ridge resembling a horn with deep grooves and a backward-projecting angle.
facts.quote: El hueso lagrimal, ubicado justo delante de los ojos, conservaba una prominente cresta rugosa, similar a un cuerno, con profundos surcos, cuyo ángulo estaba proyectado hacia atrás.

facts.statement: The nasal bone was very rough and wrinkled, with rugosities covering its entire upper surface.
facts.quote: El hueso nasal era muy áspero y arrugado. Estas rugosidades cubrían toda la superficie superior del hueso.

facts.statement: The supraorbital bone, located above the eye socket between the lacrimal and postorbital bones, gave the impression of a projecting cornice.
facts.quote: El hueso supraorbital, justo por encima de la cuenca ocular, se encontraba en medio del hueso lagrimal y postorbital, dando la impresión de una cornisa sobresaliente.

facts.statement: The area where the jaw articulated with the skull was positioned further back relative to the occipital condyle than in other theropods.
facts.quote: El área de la mandíbula que articulaba con el cráneo se encontraba más atrás del cóndilo occipital, donde el cuello se unía al cráneo, que en otros terópodos.

facts.statement: The dentary bone of the lower jaw was expanded and flattened in the area of the mandibular symphysis.
facts.quote: El dentario, hueso delantero de mandíbula inferior, se encontraba ampliado y aplanado en el área de la sínfisis mandibular.

facts.statement: The lower part of the dentary was concave due to a slight bony projection pointing downward at its tip, known as a "chin".
facts.quote: La parte inferior del dentario era cóncavo, esto se debía a que contaba con una leve proyección ósea orientada hacia abajo en su punta inferior, denominado como "barbilla".

facts.statement: The inner face of the dentary had a row of interdental plates, each providing a basin for a tooth to anchor into the jaw.
facts.quote: La cara interna del dentario tenía una fila de placas interdentales, donde cada diente tenía una cuenca para poder anclarse a la mandíbula.

facts.statement: The natural curve of the dentary suggests that the mouth of Giganotosaurus would have been wide.
facts.quote: La curva natural del dentario muestra que la boca de Giganotosaurus habría sido ancha.

facts.statement: It is possible that each dentary bone possessed twelve tooth sockets.
facts.quote: Es posible que cada dentario haya poseído doce alvéolos dentarios.

facts.statement: Most of the tooth sockets were approximately 3.5 centimeters in size.
facts.quote: La mayoría de los alvéolos eran de alrededor de 3,5 cm.

facts.statement: In the video game "Ark: Survival Evolved", Giganotosaurus is depicted as the largest and most dangerous carnivore, with dimensions exaggerated to be larger than Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: En el MMOG "Ark: Survival Evolved" es el carnívoro más grande y peligroso del juego. Sus dimensiones han sido exageradas, pues se le sitúa por encima de Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: In the video games Dino Crisis 2 and its sequel, Giganotosaurus is presented with excessive dimensions, standing about 7 meters tall and reaching 20 meters in length.
facts.quote: En el videojuego Dino Crisis 2 y en su continuación se lo presenta con dimensiones excesivas (unos 7 metros de alto y 20 de longitud).
